To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the damage pattern in the mouse liver after vincristine administration is characterized by a marked increase in autophagic vacuoles and VLDL-like vesicles, as well as by the presence of numerous alterations in the inter- and intracellular junctions, including hypertrophy, polymorphism, and irregular arrangement of gap junctions and a decrease in the tight junctions.
vincristine causes damage to the intercellular tight junctions and gap junctions in the mouse liver.

vincristine sulfate induces alterations in the mouse-liver ultrastructure, which include an increase in autophagic vacuoles and vesicles with very-low-density lipoprotein-like structures, enlargement and polymorphism of the mitochondria, dilatation of the sinusoids and bile canaliculus, penetration of lanthanum into the bile canaliculus and alterations in the inter- and intracellular junctions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ultrastructural changes in mouse liver following a single administration.
the ultrastructural changes induced by vincristine in mouse liver and their relationship to the mechanism of action of the drug.
ultrastructural alterations in the liver following vincristines administration, with special emphasis on the intercellular tight and gap junctions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alterations in the liver are due to the toxic effect of vincristine.
the alterations observed are not specific for vincristine.
the alterations are the result of the combined effects of vincristin on microtubular structures and on the cell membranes of hepatocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vincristine causes a wide variety of changes in the liver.
the alterations in the liver following vincristines administration are not restricted to the cytoplasmic organelles, but are also seen at the level of the intercellular spaces and tight junctions.
the damage to the liver cells is not limited to the cytoskeleton.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the liver is a target organ for vincristine, and the drug-induced damage pattern is similar to that observed following administration of other cytotoxic agents such as cyclophosphamide, 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide and 4-aminocyclophosphamid.
the liver is a sensitive organ to the action of vincristine.
the alterations in the junctional complexes are of primary importance.
